clue.text: Finally defeated, like Granny Smith examining mail?

definitions.meaning: beaten right at the finishing line, at the very last moment
a Granny Smith apple has pips, so it is pipped, and someone reading the mail is at the post

explanation.surface: An old lady going through her letters is somehow beaten at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: Granny Smith is an apple variety, so 'pipped' (containing pips), and reading letters puts it 'at the post'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a runner overtaken at the finishing post, hence any narrow last-moment loss.

clue.text: One who studies Lima's head of state, perhaps?

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru, so Lima stands for the country, Peru's
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as British head of state

explanation.surface: A riddle about who governs from the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima's' stands for its country by metonymy; the 'perhaps' flags that indirect step. ER is the usual crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read carefully, so a reader who studies a text closely is a peruser.

clue.text: Bloomer made by church congregations, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the congregations is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a minister's congregation is his flock; several of them are flocks

explanation.surface: Someone asks which flower the parishioners grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or an undergarment, but here it is simply something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden plant grown for its clusters of flowers, so it is a flowering plant or bloomer.

clue.text: Not appear to hear woman's concealing a deterioration

indicators.note: concealing means the woman's name wraps around and hides the next letter

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name; with the possessive it is Eve's
a drop is a fall or decline in level or quality

explanation.surface: A woman hides some decline in her hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is idiomatic: to listen secretly is to hear without appearing to be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening secretly to others' conversation means hearing them while seeming absent.

clue.text: Part of popular northern river

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stretch of a well-loved river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the Italian waterway flowing through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Support article identifying problem in infancy

parts.note: a tee is the small peg supporting a golf ball
an article is an item or thing

explanation.surface: A piece of gear is found to be the cause of a baby's trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identifying' is only a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies suffer discomfort as their first teeth come through, a classic infant complaint.

clue.text: Half of them satisfied a tourist in Cornwall

indicators.note: Half of picks out the latter two of the four letters of the word them

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, so satisfied is met

explanation.surface: A Cornish visitor pleased half of the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county at the far south-west tip of England, popular with holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornish dialect an emmet (literally an ant) is the local word for a visiting holidaymaker.

clue.text: Tyrant's papers in surprisingly poor binding

indicators.note: binding means the rearranged letters wrap around the newspapers
surprisingly tells us the letters of poor turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A dictator's newspapers are surprisingly badly bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' reads as how the papers are bound, but signals a container round the anagram 'surprisingly' makes; the 's of 'Tyrant's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is a cruel ruler who keeps people down, much as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Crime near to failing, going to arrest head of state?

indicators.note: going to arrest means the jumbled letters hold another letter captive inside them
failing suggests the words near to collapsing into a new order
head of takes just the opening letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Someone close to collapse is about to seize the leader of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' makes TREAON from NEAR TO, and 'going to arrest' puts the S of 'state' inside it. Seizing a head of state would itself be treason.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the gravest offence against one's country or sovereign, a serious crime.

clue.text: Aptness of the French leaders replacing clubs in survey

indicators.note: replacing means one letter of the survey word is swapped out for the new pieces

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, a survey of ground
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
le is French for the
the van is the front or leading part, as of an army

explanation.surface: How fitting it is that French leaders swap clubs for a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: One C of RECCE gives way to LE + VAN, leaving RE-LEVAN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is how pertinent or fitting something is, close to aptness.

clue.text: Wood a female detective identified right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is sent off from the detective's name

parts.note: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's elderly female sleuth

explanation.surface: A woman sleuth immediately recognised which kind of timber it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately' but splits: R is right, 'away' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood timber prized for furniture and flooring.

clue.text: Live with son, discriminating against women?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to live is to exist

explanation.surface: Living with a boy makes someone biased against women, it is suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexist person shows prejudice on grounds of gender, typically against women.

clue.text: Security devices placed in front of lights

definitions.text: Security devices placed in front of lights

parts.words: Security devices placed in front of lights
parts.note: lights are windows, and hinged panels closed across them keep a house secure

explanation.surface: Safety gadgets fitted ahead of the lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' looks like lamps, but in old usage a light is a window or pane.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutters are hinged panels fixed over windows to secure and darken a room.

clue.text: Distiller's vessel making a comeback

definitions.meaning: a glass flask with a long bent neck, used in distilling
a sharp reply to a remark

explanation.surface: A distilling flask staging a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' suggests a return to form; read 'comeback' as a quick answer instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a laboratory flask for distillation, and a quick witty reply.

clue.text: Wrong involving workers attached to the Italian plant

indicators.note: involving means the legal wrong takes the workers inside it

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are workers, hands
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An error involving staff attached to an Italian factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, a wild plant.

clue.text: Quietly leaves drink one's oddly not selected

indicators.note: leaves means the quiet letter departs from the drink's word

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters of one's are arranged in a strange order

parts.note: one's, with its apostrophe dropped, gives the four letters needed

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly abandons their drink, which was strangely never picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes P from PUNCH to leave UNCH, and 'oddly' turns ONES into OSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchosen has been passed over, never picked.

clue.text: Thick-skinned types welcoming creditor with a spiced wine

indicators.note: welcoming means the animals take the other letters in among them

parts.note: hippos are pachyderms, famously thick-skinned
CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor

explanation.surface: Insensitive people greet a lender with a mulled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned types' sounds like insensitive people but means hippopotamuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras was a medieval drink of wine sweetened and flavoured with spices.

clue.text: Crotchety being going over his novel

indicators.note: in a down clue going over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a being who lives is a liver

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of his take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered creature rereads his book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes ISH from HIS. Liverish means irritable, once blamed on a disordered liver.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish describes someone irritable and peevish, as if suffering a bilious liver.

clue.text: Angels the writer's represented with English harps, perhaps

indicators.note: represented means the letters are presented again in a different form

parts.note: the writer is the setter; the writer's here means the writer is, I'M

explanation.surface: An author depicts heavenly beings with harps, as they are often pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' signals the anagram; 'perhaps' admits that harps are only one way angels are pictured, and 'the writer's' is the setter saying 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Reportedly contemplate pellet gastropod mollusc

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word for looking at is heard, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: to see something is to look at or consider it
a slug is a bullet or pellet

explanation.surface: A news item about considering firing a shot at a snail-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'pellet in gastropod mollusc'; 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea slug is a shell-less marine snail, a gastropod mollusc.

clue.text: Wearing rings, left for city

indicators.note: Wearing means the rings sit around the word for left, like clothing

parts.note: each O is shaped like a ring, so rings gives two O letters
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Wearing jewellery, someone departs for town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as departed, but it is the nautical side, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the Portuguese city famed for its fortified wine.

clue.text: Manage to upset vicar in old diocese

indicators.note: in means the overturned clergyman sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the clergyman's title is turned upside down

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman such as a vicar

explanation.surface: A bishop's territory where someone succeeds in annoying the parish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where the clergyman's title is flipped to read upwards; 'in' then places it between the old diocese letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or run something, much as a manager does.

clue.text: Old PM's requirement rejected by sailor king

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
ER, Edwardus Rex, stands for King Edward

indicators.note: rejected means the necessity is turned back, and by sets it after the other pieces

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A former premier's demand is turned down by a royal seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Aberdeen was a British prime minister in the 1850s. The 's of 'PM's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Aberdeen led the British government in the 1850s, a prime minister of long ago.

clue.text: Southern states long without possible cricket team

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the yearning word goes around the team

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, die
a cricket side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Southern states pine with no prospect of a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is a nickname for the southern states of the USA.

clue.text: Timid person consuming second dessert

indicators.note: consuming means the shy person swallows a letter inside

parts.note: a mouse is a shy, timid person

explanation.surface: A shy person eats a second pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousse is a light whipped pudding often served as a sweet course.

clue.text: One dividing charitable donations' up in Indian city

indicators.note: dividing means the letter for one splits the other word apart
in a down clue up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone splits up charity takings in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ALMS into SMLA, then 'dividing' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Simla, now Shimla, was the summer capital of British India.

clue.text: Article about drama soon to be written

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the drama word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
No, or Noh, is traditional Japanese drama

explanation.surface: A piece concerning a play that will shortly be written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be written' is surface padding linking the definition; the old word 'anon' means shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or presently.

clue.text: Synthetic product recent divorcee talked of

indicators.note: talked of says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a recent ex is a late ex, a former spouse only lately divorced

explanation.surface: Someone discussed an artificial material made by a newly divorced person.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky rubber base, now often made synthetically for gloves and paints.

clue.text: Donkey that's amusing, or otherwise?

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are put in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Is a donkey funny, or not?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkey' here is a fool, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, stupid person, which donkey can mean informally.

clue.text: Award one in Drake's ship's exchanged for a fish

indicators.note: exchanged for means the letter for one is swapped out for the letter A

parts.note: the Golden Hind was Sir Francis Drake's ship; with the possessive it ends in S
I is the Roman numeral one
hake is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A prize: one on Drake's vessel was swapped for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the I in GOLDENHINDS to A, then add HAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a generous payment given on leaving a job, a parting award.
